extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) staff, and other USPTO personnel handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for preparing, reviewing, and issuing ex parte reexamination certificates, including treatment of multiple dependent claims, examiner amendments, reasons for patentability, checklist completion, certificate format, distribution, and reexamination-of-reexamination processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of multiple dependent claims for NIRC and certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: How additions, deletions, and changes to multiple dependent claims are characterized for purposes of the Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) and the Examiner’s checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition of a claim of the multiple dependency is viewed as adding a new claim (designated 'new' in the NIRC) because new subject matter/protection is provided (example: claim 2/8 designated new). Deletion of a claim of the multiple dependency is viewed as canceling the deleted claim (designated 'canceled' in the NIRC). A claim whose text or scope changes (e.g., range expanded) is designated as 'amended.' For the Examiner’s checklist (Form PTO-1516), however, the addition or deletion of a claim of the multiple dependency is viewed simply as amending the claim because of the way claims are printed on the certificate; thus such claims are designated as 'amended' on the checklist and printed in their amended form on the certificate. Provide concrete examples (claims 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 in the guidance) to reflect these conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical cancellation of live claims in file history
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for physically marking canceled live patent claims in the file history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place brackets around all the live claims on a copy of the claims printed from the file history and scan that copy into the IFW file history. Ensure all other claims in the proceeding have been previously replaced or canceled. Examiner will designate a cancelled original patent claim to be printed in the Official Gazette via the Issue Classification IFW form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion and reporting of claim status on NIRC (PTOL-469) and Examiner checklist (PTO-1516)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to report confirmed, amended, canceled, and new claims on the NIRC and the examiner’s checklists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 1(h) of PTOL-469 and relevant items of PTO-1516 must be completed to reflect the status of claims (e.g., 'Patent claims confirmed', 'Patent claims amended', 'Patent claims canceled', 'New claims patentable'). Use the Examiner’s checklist parts directed to claim status (items 12-14 etc.) to indicate patent claims amended, dependent-on-amended status, and new patentable claims. Where multiple-dependent claim additions/deletions occur, decide designations consistent with the 'treatment of multiple dependent claims' guidance above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for patentability and/or confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to provide reasons explaining why claims found patentable or confirmed are patentable over cited patents/printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for patentability must be provided unless all claims are canceled in the proceeding. Check Box 2 of PTOL-469 and attach a statement (may use form PTOL-476 or preferred form paragraph 22.16) indicating why the claims found patentable are clearly patentable over the cited patents/printed publications; this may be done in a manner similar to reasons for allowance in an application and may refer to record portions that establish patentability. Any 'Comments on Statement of Reasons for Patentability and/or Confirmation' received from the patent owner will be placed in the reexamination file without comment and may be considered if timely submitted to avoid processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of submissions after issuance of NIRC
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for consideration of amendments, IDSs, or other merits-related papers filed after a NIRC has been issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.182 does not apply automatically in reexamination. Any amendment, information disclosure statement, or other merits-related paper filed after issuance of the NIRC must be accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182. The petition must be granted for the submission to be considered. If granted, the examiner will reconsider the case and, if appropriate, reopen prosecution. See MPEP § 2256 for criteria for obtaining entry and consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination reminders — scope and substantive examination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All patent claims for which a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) has been found must have been examined before the case is forwarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every claim identified with an SNQ has been properly examined in accordance with MPEP § 2243 prior to forwarding the case for issuance of certificate or other final actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination reminders — renumbering prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in reexamination proceedings may not be renumbered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New claims may require renumbering (of new claims themselves), but renumbering of patent claims is not permitted. See MPEP § 2250.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination reminders — conformity of amendments to 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j)
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments to description and claims must conform to the statutory/regulatory presentation and marking requirements for amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes changes made by Examiner’s Amendment. If a portion of text is amended more than once, each amendment should indicate all changes (insertions and deletions) relative to the current patent text under reexamination. See MPEP § 2250 and 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination reminders — prior art listing forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art cited in the reexamination must be listed on approved PTO forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prior art must be listed on form PTO 892, PTO/SB/08A or 08B, or PTO/SB/42, or on a form having an equivalent format. These forms must be properly completed. See MPEP § 2257.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination reminders — completion of examiner and clerical checklists (PTO-1516, PTO-1517)
rubrics_metrics.description: Both examiner and reexamination clerical checklists must be fully and properly completed and cross-checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A careful reading of instructions in these checklists is essential. The clerical checklist is a check and review of the examiner’s responses; CRU support staff should personally review the file before completing items and ensure related items on both checklists agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination reminders — merging of multiple pending reexaminations
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple pending reexamination proceedings are often merged and must be handled per rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that merging is common; see MPEP § 2283 for guidance on merging proceedings and implications for file processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination reminders — co-pending reissue applications and OPLA referral
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reexamination proceeding is copending with a reissue application, forward files to OPLA for merger consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward files to the Office of Patent Legal Administration (OPLA) for consideration of potential merger, and ensure a Senior Legal Advisor's decision on the merger question is present in the reexamination file. See MPEP § 2285.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination reminders — requirement of reasons for each patentable/confirmed claim
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must provide reasons for patentability/confirmation for each claim found patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons are required for each claim found patentable and/or confirmed. See section on 'Reasons for Patentability and/or Confirmation' for format and form paragraph options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination reminders — issue fee and expired-patent limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: No issue fee is charged in reexamination; claims cannot be amended or new claims added after patent expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no issue fee in reexamination (see MPEP § 2233). Patent claims may not be amended nor new claims added after expiration of the patent (see MPEP § 2250). If the patent has expired, all amendments and claims added during the proceeding must be withdrawn and presently rejected/objected-to claims canceled by examiner’s amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination reminders — drawings/drawings amendments handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Original drawings cannot be physically changed; amended/new figures must be presented correctly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original drawings cannot be physically changed. 'Amended' or 'New' figures must be appropriately labeled and presented on new sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.84. See 37 CFR 1.530(d)(3) and MPEP § 2250.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte reexamination reminders — no enlargement of claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An amended or new claim may not enlarge the scope of the patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure amendments and new claims do not broaden claim scope. See MPEP § 2250.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s Amendment requirements in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and required content when examiner prepares an amendment to place the proceeding in condition for issuance of a reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may request patent owner provide amendments or make amendments with patent owner's approval via a formal examiner’s amendment. Examiner’s amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j). The full text of any paragraph or claim to be changed must be presented with 37 CFR 1.530(f) markings. The exception in 37 CFR 1.121(g) does not apply. The only exception to full-text presentation is that an entire claim or an entire paragraph may be deleted by a statement deleting it without presentation of its text. If the patent expires during the proceeding, all amendments made during the proceeding are improper and must be expressly withdrawn by statement in the examiner’s amendment. When preparing an examiner’s amendment, draw diagonal lines across copies of all amended/new claims and text added, and scan into IFW; check Box 7 of PTOL-469 and use form paragraph 22.06 to attach the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format, numbering, and content conventions for ex parte reexamination certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: How ex parte reexamination certificates are formatted, numbered, and what content they include.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate titled 'Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate' followed by an ordinal number in parentheses (e.g., '(235th)'). Certificate number equals original patent number plus a two-character kind-code suffix: first letter 'B' for certificates published before Jan 2, 2001, 'C' for on/after Jan 2, 2001; second letter is the reexamination proceeding number for that patent (shows how many times reexamined). Certificates will denote date at INID code [45], include title, inventor, classifications, abstract, list of prior art (available via PAIR by reexam control number), and will identify claims confirmed, canceled, disclaimed, and not examined. Text of new claims printed completely in italics; amended claims printed with italics and bracketing indicating amendments. Prior court decisions and citations will be identified. A notice of the issuance will be published in the Official Gazette on date of issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and effects of ex parte reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal and substantive effects and required contents of the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 35 U.S.C. 307 and 37 CFR 1.570, the certificate will: (A) cancel any patent claims determined unpatentable; (B) confirm any patent claims determined patentable; (C) incorporate into the patent any amended or new claims determined patentable; (D) make any approved changes in the description; (E) include any statutory or terminal disclaimer filed by the patent owner; (F) identify unamended claims held invalid on final holding by another forum; (G) identify any patent claims not reexamined; (H) be mailed on its date to the patent owner (and a copy to the requester); and (I) identify patent claims dependent on amended claims determined patentable. If certificate cancels all claims, no further Office proceedings on that patent or related reissue/reexamination requests will be conducted (with rare exceptions allowing petition under 37 CFR 1.183).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination review and quality assurance before certificate issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal review processes for reexamination cases to ensure correct practice and preparation prior to certificate issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination cases are monitored and reviewed in CRU or Technology Center by CRU SPRS or TC QAS, paralegal or backup support at multiple prosecution stages. Panel review is made prior to issuing Office actions (MPEP § 2271.01). After NIRC and termination of prosecution, cases undergo OPLA screening for obvious errors and proper preparation before issuance. These reviews correct errors, identify problem areas/trends, and provide feedback on uniformity of practice. CRU/OPLA reviews are vehicles for final quality assurance prior to issuing certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: How reexamination certificates are distributed and recorded after issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An e-copy of the certificate will be associated with the e-copy of the patent in the search files; a copy will be made part of any patent copies prepared by the Office after issuance. A copy will be forwarded to all depository libraries and to foreign offices with exchange agreements with the USPTO. Files of proceedings that were denied/vacated receive processing for partial refund per 37 CFR 1.26(c) and status annotation (420/422).

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening rights resulting from reexamination certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of newly incorporated amended or new claims on intervening rights of third parties who acted prior to certificate issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 35 U.S.C. 307(b), any proposed amended or new claim determined patentable and incorporated into a patent by certificate will have the same effect as specified in 35 U.S.C. 252 for reissued patents regarding rights of persons who made, purchased, used, imported, or substantially prepared for the thing patented prior to issuance of the certificate. See cited cases for precedent (Fortel, Kaufman, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ways ex parte reexamination proceedings conclude and processing consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible dispositions for concluding an ex parte reexamination proceeding and corresponding processing steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings may conclude by: (A) denial of reexamination, vacating, or termination (no certificate issued); (B) issuance of a Reexamination Certificate under 37 CFR 1.570(b); (C) merged with reissue where reissue patent serves as certificate (37 CFR 1.570(e)); or (D) merged with inter partes reexamination with a single certificate issued (37 CFR 1.997(b)). Processing steps include CRU/SPRS/QAS review, forwarding to OPLA, and following MPEP sections specific to merged dispositions. For proceedings concluded by denial/vacation, process file for partial refund if applicable and annotate PALM/IFW as 'PROCEEDING CONCLUDED.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing a reexamination of a reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle a reexamination request filed on a patent already subject to a reexamination certificate or on which a prior reexamination certificate has issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the request based on the patent claims as modified by the previously issued reexamination certificate, not the original claims. When the new reexamination is first received by CRU, support staff must incorporate certificate changes into the reexamination specification before forwarding to the examiner. Examiner should verify the certificate changes entry and base the order/denial decision on the certificate-modified claims/specification. If a first reexamination certificate will issue within ~3 months of filing a second request, proceedings normally will not be merged; the second request will be considered based on the claims as indicated in the issued certificate if the certificate issues before decision on the second request. Include copy of the reexamination certificate as attachment to the order/denial decision for third-party requesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of certificate issuance in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: What the Official Gazette notice for an ex parte reexamination certificate must include and emphasize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice will include bibliographic information, an indication of the status of each claim after conclusion, and publication of a representative claim with any specification/drawing changes indicated. The notice will clearly indicate that it is a certificate for a concluded ex parte reexamination proceeding as opposed to an inter partes proceeding.
